title: Field with its own contract: seen factor, second-order terms, fall and clock

key_results.statement: Class: every member of $\mathcal D$ and every nondegenerate eigenvector $\varphi_0$ of $C_f$, $\varepsilon=0$ or $\varepsilon>0$; regime: none (R0); status: exact. $\hat C=\hat C_b\otimes\mathbb 1_c+\sum_xP_x\otimes\kappa xX$ with $\hat C_b=A+\sum_xP_x\otimes[N(x)\sigma_3\otimes(m+D)+e_0]$, the member of $\mathcal C$ with $\zeta_x=1$, $m_x=mN(x)$, $\eta_x=N(x)$, $V_x=e_0$; $\hat C$ is the contract of an admissible description of $b$ and $c$.

Class $\mathcal D$, R0, exact: under (2.20) $N(x)\to N(x)+a_x$, $e_0\to e_0+c$, while $\varphi_0$, $\tilde\Phi_x$, $S$, $\varepsilon_x$, $\Delta_f$, $\nu$ and $\hat C$ are unchanged; $N(x)$ is well defined only together with the coefficient of $B_x$ in $C_{br}$ (zero in the form of $\mathcal D$).
Class $\mathcal D$, every start of the body, R0; status: bound, all $\lambda\ge0$: $\lVert(\mathbb 1-\Pi_0)\Psi(\lambda)\rVert\le\varepsilon M_{\max}\lambda$.

Class $\mathcal D$; regime R1: $2\epsilon_1+2\epsilon_2+\epsilon_3<1$ with $\epsilon_3=\nu M_{\max}/\Delta_f$, weak records (a sufficient condition, not shown to be necessary); status: order estimate of the constant, all $\lambda\ge0$: $\lVert(\mathbb 1-\Pi_0)\Psi(\lambda)\rVert\le2\epsilon_1[1+O(\epsilon_1^2+\epsilon_2+\epsilon_3)]$; for $\varepsilon=0$ the left side is zero.

Class $\mathcal D$, every schedule of readings on $b$ and $c$: bound $\sum\lvert p-\hat p\rvert\le2\varepsilon M_{\max}\lambda_k$ in R0; in R1 (order estimate, fixed schedule) $\sum\lvert p-\hat p\rvert=O(\epsilon_1^2)+O(\epsilon_1^2\Delta_f\lambda_k)$, so the statistics are those of a sharp field with the profile $N(x)$ through first order in $\epsilon_1$ on $\lambda\ll1/(\epsilon_1^2\Delta_f)$.

Class $\mathcal D$, regime R1: $H_{\rm eff}=\hat C-\tfrac12(\mathcal S_1^{\dagger}W_1+W_1^{\dagger}\mathcal S_1)+O(\epsilon_1^4\Delta_f)$ with $\mathcal S_1$ the solution of the Sylvester equation; for the exact $H_{\rm eff}$, $\lVert\Pi_0\Psi(\lambda)-(e^{-iH_{\rm eff}\lambda}(\phi\otimes\chi))\otimes\varphi_0\rVert\le2\epsilon_1^2[1+\dots]$ for all $\lambda\ge0$ (order estimate of the constant).

Class $\mathcal D$, regime R1, status: exact coefficient of the second order in $\epsilon_1$ at leading order in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$: $H^{(2)}=-\sum_x\gamma_xP_x\otimes\mathbb 1_2\otimes(m+D)^2\otimes\mathbb 1_c$ with $\gamma_x=\langle\varphi_0\vert\tilde\Phi_xS\tilde\Phi_x\vert\varphi_0\rangle$, $\lvert\gamma_x\rvert\le\varepsilon_x^2/\Delta_f$.

Class $\mathcal D$, regime R1, status: exact first corrections with an order estimate of the remainder $O(\epsilon_1^2(\epsilon_2+\epsilon_3)^2\Delta_f)+O(\epsilon_1^4\Delta_f)$: $H^{(2,1)}=-\tfrac\tau2\sum_x(c_xh_x\otimes(-i\sigma_1)+c_x^{*}h_x^{\dagger}\otimes(i\sigma_1))\otimes\mathcal M^2$ with $c_x=\tfrac12(\rho_{xx}+\rho_{x+1,x+1})+\rho_{x+1,x}$, and $H^{(3)}=\sum_x\gamma^{(3)}_xP_x\otimes\sigma_3\otimes\mathcal M^3$; $\hat C+H^{(2)}$ reproduces the statistics to accuracy $\eta\gg\epsilon_1^2$ for $\lambda\lesssim\eta/[\epsilon_1^2\Delta_f(\epsilon_2+\epsilon_3+\epsilon_1^2)]$.

Class $\mathcal D$, regime R1, second order in $\epsilon_1$ with first corrections: on the level $k$ the on-site block is $(N(x)M_k+\gamma^{(3)}_xM_k^3)\sigma_3+(e_0-\gamma_xM_k^2)\mathbb 1_2$ and the hopping block is $-\tfrac{i\tau}2(1-M_k^2c_x)\sigma_1$; at leading order in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$ the body part of $\hat C+H^{(2)}$ is a member of $\mathcal C_{\rm lev}$ for every member of $\mathcal D$, and of $\mathcal C$ iff $\gamma_x=0$ for all $x$; the hopping phase is moved by a unitary into the start; all new terms are well defined under (2.20).

Class $\mathcal D$, regime R1: with $\mu_{x,k}=N(x)M_k+\gamma^{(3)}_xM_k^3$, the body part with the first corrections is a member of $\mathcal C_{\rm lev}$ up to the hopping phase if and only if (P): $\mu_{x,k}>0$ for all $x,k$; margin (P') against the remainder of (10.10); $\varepsilon\epsilon_1\epsilon_3<\min_xN(x)$ is sufficient for (P); R1 does not imply (P) (two-place control with $a<0$); where $\mu_{x,k}<0$ the upper on-site eigenvalue is $V_{x,k}-\mu_{x,k}$.

Class: linear profiles $\Phi_x=N_0+xY$; regime R1, second order in $\epsilon_1$, first corrections in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$, first order in $Y$; status: closed forms: $\tau_k=\tau(1-2\rho_0M_k^2)$, $\hat M_k=M_k(1+\gamma^{(3)}_0M_k^2)$, $G_k=gM_k+\gamma^{(3)}_1M_k^3$, $\mathcal F_k=\gamma_1M_k^2$, $g_{\zeta,k}=-4M_k^2\operatorname{Re}\rho_Y$, $V_k=e_0-\gamma_0M_k^2$; level data of a member of $\mathcal C_{\rm lev}$ at leading order for the whole class, with the first corrections under (10.28); a level offset is a common phase for a start in one level.

Class: linear profiles, regime R1, first corrections: the level data (10.12) are those of a member of $\mathcal C_{\rm lev}$ on $\lvert x\rvert\le L$ if and only if $\hat M_k>\lvert G_k\rvert L$ and $\lvert g_{\zeta,k}\rvert(L-\tfrac12)<1$ for all $k$; margins $(\lvert\gamma^{(3)}_0\rvert+\lvert\gamma^{(3)}_1\rvert L)M_{\max}^2\ll1-\lvert g\rvert L$ and $M_0(1-\lvert g\rvert L)\gg\epsilon_1^2[(\epsilon_2+\epsilon_3)^2+\epsilon_1^2]\Delta_f$; R1 does not imply it.

Class: linear profiles, branch starts at rest, $\langle X\rangle=0$; regime R1 as (10.12), drift acceleration in the description with $H_{\rm eff}$; status: closed form: $a_{k,\sigma}(0)=\tau^2[-g+\sigma\gamma_1M_k+\beta M_k^2]$, $\beta=g(4\rho_0+\gamma^{(3)}_0)-\gamma^{(3)}_1$; the term in $\gamma_1$ is exact at leading order in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$ for the whole class and not small against $g$ in R1; the term in $\beta$ holds under (10.28).

Class and regime of (10.13), $\langle X\rangle=0$, under (10.28); status: exact in the level data: $a_{k,\sigma}(0)=\tau^2\frac{(1-2\rho_0M_k^2)^2}{1+\gamma^{(3)}_0M_k^2}[-g+\sigma\gamma_1M_k-\gamma^{(3)}_1M_k^2]$; the term in $\beta$ of (10.13) exceeds the terms dropped only if $\lvert\gamma_1\rvert M_k(\epsilon_1^2+\lvert\gamma^{(3)}_0\rvert M_k^2)\ll\lvert\beta\rvert M_k^2$, in particular for $\gamma_1=0$.

Class and regime of (10.13), $\langle X\rangle=0$: at leading order in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$ and every $N\ge2$, level-independence of $a_{k,+}(0)$, of $a_{k,-}(0)$ and of both with the one value $-\tau^2g$ each hold iff $\gamma_1=0$ (exact leading-order expression); for the expression (10.13) with the first corrections, under (10.28): $N\ge3$ iff $\gamma_1=0$ and $\beta=0$; $N=2$ upper iff $\gamma_1+\beta(M_0+M_1)=0$, lower iff $\gamma_1-\beta(M_0+M_1)=0$, both iff $\gamma_1=\beta=0$.

Class: linear profiles, branch starts at rest, every $\langle X\rangle$; regime R1, leading order in $\kappa$ with the plain gradient $-\kappa\langle X\rangle$ kept; closed form: $a_{k,\sigma}(0)=\tau^2[-g+\sigma\gamma_1M_k+\beta M_k^2]+a^{\rm rec}_{k,\sigma}$, $a^{\rm rec}_{k,\sigma}=-\sigma\tau_k^2\kappa\langle X\rangle/\hat M_k$; the record term is of zeroth order in $\epsilon_1$, odd in the branch and different for every two levels when $\langle X\rangle\neq0$; terms in $\beta$, $\rho_0$, $\gamma^{(3)}_0$ under (10.28).

Class and regime of (10.22), $\langle X\rangle\neq0$: at leading order in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$ the fall from rest is level-dependent in each branch for $N\ge3$, and for $N=2$ level-independent in one branch iff $\gamma_1M_0M_1=-\kappa\langle X\rangle$; for the expression (10.22) with the first corrections, under (10.28), level-dependent in each branch for $N\ge4$, with exceptional members for $N=3$ and $N=2$; for every $N\ge2$ independence in both branches with one value implies $\langle X\rangle=0$.

Class: linear profiles, branch starts $B_{k,\sigma}[g]$, under (10.28); regime R1, zero gradients with the uniform hopping phase $\theta_k=M_k^2\operatorname{Im}\rho_Y$, first order in $\theta_k$; exact coefficient in the description with $H_{\rm eff}$: $\mathrm d\bar x_{\rm lab}/\mathrm d\lambda=\sigma\langle\omega_k'\rangle_g+v^{\rm ph}_{k,\sigma}(\lambda)$ with $v^{\rm ph}_{k,\sigma}$ bounded for all $\lambda$, so the drift accelerations are unchanged at first order in $Y$.

Class: linear profiles, branch starts at rest, under (10.28); regime R1, second order in $\epsilon_1$, first order in $\epsilon_2$ and in $Y$; a velocity, not a drift acceleration: sharp label at fixed $\lambda$: $v^{\rm ph}_{k,\sigma}(\lambda)=-\sigma\tau^2M_k\operatorname{Im}\rho_Y[1-\cos(2M_k\lambda)]$; long window: $\bar v^{\rm ph}_{k,\sigma}=-\sigma\tau^2M_k\operatorname{Im}\rho_Y$; the growth of $\lambda$ and the sharp label do not commute for the velocity itself; it vanishes iff $\operatorname{Im}\rho_Y=0$ and is otherwise different for every two levels.

Class: every member of $\mathcal D$, every $x$; regime R1, second order in $\epsilon_1$, leading order plus the first correction in $\epsilon_3$; a polynomial identity: $E^+_{x,k+1}-E^+_{x,k}=\frac{2\pi}{N\lambda_0}[N(x)-\gamma_x(M_k+M_{k+1})+\gamma^{(3)}_x(M_k^2+M_kM_{k+1}+M_{k+1}^2)]$; $E^+_{x,k}$ is the on-site eigenvalue of the branch place $s=1$, the upper one with the cubic term iff $\mu_{x,k}>0$; a difference can vanish or be negative in R1.

Class $\mathcal D$, every $x$, regime R1: the differences (10.15) are independent of $k$ at leading order in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$ iff $N=2$ or $\gamma_x=0$; with the first corrections iff $N=2$, or $N=3$ and $\gamma_x=3\gamma^{(3)}_xM_1$, or $N\ge4$ and $\gamma_x=\gamma^{(3)}_x=0$.

Class: linear profiles, starts $S_{\rm clock}(x_0)$; regime R1 at leading order in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$ and at the orders of (3.36) (zeroth order in the gradients); order estimate: the clock statistics is the mixture (3.36) with every advance shifted by $-\gamma_{x_0}\Sigma\lambda/\lambda_0$ (one rate $\bar r(x_0)=[N(x_0)-\gamma_{x_0}\Sigma]/\lambda_0$ only in the wide-start limit) up to total variation $\le\tfrac12\lvert\gamma_{x_0}\rvert d_{N-1}^2\lambda$; accuracy $\eta$ for $\lambda\le2\eta/(\lvert\gamma_{x_0}\rvert d_{N-1}^2)$ if $N\ge3$, $\gamma_{x_0}\neq0$; otherwise no deviation at this order.

Ring clock with the one rate $r\in\mathbb R$: clock label in $N^{-1/2}\sum_ke^{-2\pi irk\lambda/N}\lvert f_k\rangle$; the mean rate $\lambda_0\bar r(x_0)=N(x_0)-\gamma_{x_0}\Sigma$ (leading order in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$) is positive, zero or negative in R1, and (10.16), (10.30) hold in each case; a ring clock with $r=0$ stands and is no reference for a ratio of rates; these are statements about the ring clock, and the clock of the body has its statistics only to the accuracy and on the range of (10.16), (10.30).

Class: linear profiles, starts $S_{\rm clock}(x_0)$, under (10.28); regime R1, second order in $\epsilon_1$ with the first correction in $\epsilon_3$, zeroth order in the gradients, wide-start limit at fixed $\lambda$, on the range of (10.10); order estimate: $\bar r(x)=\lambda_0^{-1}[N(x)-\gamma_x\Sigma+\gamma^{(3)}_x(M_0^2+M_0M_{N-1}+M_{N-1}^2)]$, $\delta E_k=d_k(d_{N-1}-d_k)[\gamma_{x_0}-\gamma^{(3)}_{x_0}(M_k+\Sigma)]$, total variation from the ring clock $\le\tfrac12\Xi_{x_0}d_{N-1}^2\lambda$; accuracy $\eta$ for $\lambda\le2\eta/(\Xi_{x_0}d_{N-1}^2)$ when $N\ge3$, $\Xi_{x_0}\neq0$.

Setting of (10.30): the mean rate is a statement on the two end levels, $E^+_{x_0,N-1}-E^+_{x_0,0}=\frac{2\pi(N-1)}{N}\bar r(x_0)$; for $\bar r(x_0)=0$ the clock label is in $N^{-1/2}\sum_ke^{-i\delta E_k\lambda}\lvert f_k\rangle$ and the clock statistics is independent of $\lambda$ iff $N=2$ or $\Xi_{x_0}=0$; at leading order in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$ and $N\ge3$, $\delta E_k=N(x_0)d_k(d_{N-1}-d_k)/\Sigma>0$ for the inner levels, so the clock label evolves; a negative mean rate states $E^+_{x_0,N-1}<E^+_{x_0,0}$ and no more.

Class: linear profiles, branch starts at rest, every $\langle X\rangle$, members with $D_0=1-\gamma_0\Sigma\neq0$ (margin of (10.35)); regime R1, leading order in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$, first order in $Y$; closed form, exact in $\gamma_0\Sigma$: relative gradient of the mean rate $(g-\gamma_1\Sigma)/D_0$ and defect $\mathcal R_k=\tau^2[\gamma_1(M_k-\Sigma/D_0)+g\gamma_0\Sigma/D_0-\kappa\langle X\rangle/M_k]$; (4.24) holds for all levels iff $\gamma_1=0$, $g\gamma_0=0$, $\langle X\rangle=0$ for $N\ge3$, and iff $\gamma_0(g-\gamma_1\Sigma)=0$, $\gamma_1M_0M_1=-\kappa\langle X\rangle$ for $N=2$.

Class and regime of (10.34): the comparison of (4.24) is defined iff $D_0\neq0$; margin (order estimate) $\lvert D_0\rvert\gg\varepsilon\epsilon_1(\epsilon_3+\epsilon_1^2+\epsilon_2^2)$; hierarchy (H): $\lvert\gamma_0\rvert\Sigma\ll1$; $2\epsilon_1\varepsilon\ll1$ is sufficient for (H) and for the margin; neither R1 nor (10.28) implies (H).

Class and regime of (10.34), $\langle X\rangle=0$, under (H) of (10.35) only: $\mathcal R_k=\tau^2[\gamma_1(M_k-\Sigma)+g\gamma_0\Sigma]$ with $\Sigma=M_0+M_{N-1}$; the leading deviation contains the data $m$, $d_{N-1}$ of the body.

Class and regime of (10.34), every $\langle X\rangle$, under (H) of (10.35) only: $\mathcal R_k=\tau^2[\gamma_1(M_k-\Sigma)+g\gamma_0\Sigma-\kappa\langle X\rangle/M_k]$; for $\langle X\rangle\neq0$ the relation (4.24) fails already at zeroth order in $\epsilon_1$, for a sharp field.

Members with a vanishing mean rate, $D_0=0$ at the order kept, exist in R1 with the margins of (10.28) (two-level, two-place control): the relative gradient at $x=0$ is not defined; $\bar r(0)a_{k,+}(0)+\tau^2[\bar r(1)-\bar r(0)]=\tau^2\bar r(1)=\tau^2(g-\gamma_1\Sigma)/\lambda_0$, so the multiplied form holds iff $g=\gamma_1\Sigma$; then the mean rate vanishes at every position, which by (10.37) makes the clock statistics stationary only for $N=2$.

Three readings of the expression of (5.11) for a hopping factor that depends on the level, at zeroth order in the gradients: level speed $v^{(k)}_{\max}=\tau_kd_0=\tau(1-2\rho_0M_k^2)d_0$ (level block); $v^{\rm pl}_{\max}=\tau d_0\sum_{a'}\lvert\langle a'\vert\mathbb 1_N-2\rho_0\mathcal M^2\vert a\rangle\rvert\ge v^{(0)}_{\max}$, with equality for $N=2$ (body part with the clock places); $v^C_{\max}=\tau d_0$ (contract $C$); only the expression is evaluated, the bound is quoted for $C_{\rm D}$.

Class: linear profiles, branch starts at rest, every $\langle X\rangle$, under (10.28) and $D_1\neq0$; regime R1, second order in $\epsilon_1$ with the first corrections, first order in $Y$; exact in the level data, no reciprocal expanded: $\varrho=(g-\gamma_1\Sigma+\gamma^{(3)}_1\Sigma_3)/D_1$, $D_1=1-\gamma_0\Sigma+\gamma^{(3)}_0\Sigma_3$, $\Sigma_3=M_0^2+M_0M_{N-1}+M_{N-1}^2$; $\mathcal R^{\rm lev}_k=\tau_k^2[\varrho+(-g+\gamma_1M_k-\gamma^{(3)}_1M_k^2-\kappa\langle X\rangle/M_k)/(1+\gamma^{(3)}_0M_k^2)]$ with the level speeds, $\mathcal R^{(w)}_k=\mathcal R^{\rm lev}_k+(w^2-\tau_k^2)\varrho$ with one speed $wd_0$; the first corrections exceed the terms dropped only in the range stated after (10.32).

Members with a vanishing leading defect ($\gamma_1=0$, $g\gamma_0=0$, $\langle X\rangle=0$, $D_0\neq0$), conditions of (10.39), equivalences for the terms kept: $\mathcal R^{\rm lev}_k=\tau_k^2[\beta_3(M_k^2-\Sigma_3)+\gamma_0\gamma^{(3)}_1\Sigma M_k^2]/[D_1(1+\gamma^{(3)}_0M_k^2)]$ with $\beta_3=g\gamma^{(3)}_0-\gamma^{(3)}_1$; for $\gamma_0=0$ the relation with the level speeds holds in all levels iff $\beta_3=0$ and in no level otherwise; for $g=0\neq\gamma_0$ in all levels iff $\gamma^{(3)}_1=0$; when it holds in all levels, $\mathcal R^{(w)}_k=(w^2-\tau_k^2)g$, so with one speed it holds for all levels iff $g\rho_0=0$ and otherwise in at most one level ($\mathcal R^{(\tau)}_k=4\tau^2g\rho_0M_k^2(1-\rho_0M_k^2)$); control: a three-place field with an inner $e_0$.

Class: independent cells, every $\Delta_x>0$, $n_x>0$, $\varepsilon_x\ge0$; regime R1 with $\epsilon_3=\epsilon_1$; exact coefficients: $N(x)=n_x$, $\varepsilon=\max_x\varepsilon_x$, $\Delta_f=\min_x\Delta_x$, $\gamma_x=\varepsilon_x^2/\Delta_x$, $\rho_{xy}=\delta_{xy}\varepsilon_x^2/\Delta_x^2$, $c_x=\tfrac12(\varepsilon_x^2/\Delta_x^2+\varepsilon_{x+1}^2/\Delta_{x+1}^2)$, $\gamma^{(3)}_x=0$; the body part is a member of $\mathcal C_{\rm lev}$ with (P) for every cell description.

Class: one cell with the body at $x$, branch sign $\pm$, level $k$; exact: eigenvalues $\pm M_kn_x-\Omega_{x,k}$ (lower) and $\pm M_kn_x+\Omega_{x,k}$ (upper), $\Omega_{x,k}=\sqrt{\Delta_x^2/4+M_k^2\varepsilon_x^2}$; overlap of the lower eigenvector with $\lvert0\rangle$: $\cos(\alpha_{x,k}/2)=[\tfrac12(1+\Delta_x/2\Omega_{x,k})]^{1/2}$; at leading order in $\tau/\Delta_x$ the hopping block is multiplied by $\cos(\alpha_{x,k}/2)\cos(\alpha_{x+1,k}/2)$.

Subclass $\mathcal L$ of the cells, the class of item 4(c): $n_x=1+gx$, $\varepsilon_x^2/\Delta_x=\gamma_0+\gamma_1x$ and $c_x=\rho_0+\rho_1(x+\tfrac12)$ for all $x$; for cells with $n_x=1+gx$ it holds iff the level profiles are linear for all levels; cells with a constant $\varepsilon_x^2/\Delta_x=\gamma$ are in $\mathcal L$ iff $\gamma=0$ or $1/\Delta_x+1/\Delta_{x+1}$ is linear in $x$.

Class: cells of $\mathcal L$, branch starts at rest, $\langle X\rangle=0$; regime R1, first order in the gradients of the cell data: $a_{k,\sigma}(0)=\tau^2[-g+\sigma\gamma_1M_k+2g\rho_0M_k^2]$; control within $\mathcal L$, constant $\gamma$: the branch-odd term vanishes, while the level offsets, the defect $\tau^2g\gamma\Sigma/(1-\gamma\Sigma)$ of (4.24) (for $\gamma\Sigma\neq1$) and the level-dependent hopping remain; for cells outside $\mathcal L$ the results of items 4(a), 4(b) hold and the fall is not stated.

Class $\mathcal D$ (linear profiles for rows 2-5), regime R1, order estimate: rows 1-4 are unchanged at order $\epsilon_1$ (rows 2, 4 for $\langle X\rangle=0$; row 3 in the wide-start limit at fixed $\lambda$ and zeroth order in the gradients); the first change is at order $\epsilon_1^2$ at the leading order of the coefficient in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$, of relative size $\lvert\gamma_x\rvert M_{\max}\le\epsilon_1\varepsilon$ (not a small number of R1), in the members in which the leading coefficient of the row is not zero, and otherwise at first order in $\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3$ or not at the orders kept; the velocity from the hopping phase appears at order $\epsilon_1^2$ and first order in $\epsilon_2$ if $\operatorname{Im}\rho_Y\neq0$.

open_issues: (10.6), the R1 part of (10.7) and the remainders of (10.10) are order estimates: their constants and the dependence of (10.7) on the number of readings are not bounded explicitly.

The accelerations (10.13), (10.20), (10.22) and the velocity (10.24), (10.25) are those of the description with H_eff; for the description with C only the agreement of the statistics within (10.10) is derived, not a statement about its acceleration or its velocity.

Members in which (P) of (10.27), or (10.28) for the linear profiles, fails or holds without its margin: the statements with the first corrections are not derived for them; the exchange of the branch places of a level with a negative rest term is not worked out, and a rest term that changes sign along the chain is not treated.

Members whose comparison rate vanishes within the margin of (10.35): the sign of the mean rate is decided by terms not kept, and neither (10.34) nor (10.36) is derived for them; the margin itself is an order estimate.

With γ_1 ≠ 0 the term τ²βM_k² of (10.13) is larger than the terms dropped after (10.32) only under the hierarchy stated there; the terms of fourth order of H_eff, of the same size as the dropped terms, are not computed.

The speeds of (10.38) are three readings of the expression of (5.11); which of them is the maximal speed of a body whose hopping factor depends on the level is not decided, because (5.11) is quoted for C_D and the bound for another body contract is not among the quoted inputs; (10.39), (10.40) are stated for each reading, the place-basis speed is not evaluated in closed form for N ≥ 3, and for a leading defect that is not zero the first corrections of (10.39) exceed the terms dropped only in the range stated after (10.32).

Outside the scope of the question: the fall from rest, the defect of (4.24) and the clock range of cells with n_x = 1 + g x whose γ_x or c_x is not linear in x; they need a result for level profiles that are not linear (a later package).

(10.16) has the orders of (3.36) (zeroth order in the gradients) and the leading order in ε_2, ε_3; (10.30) holds in the wide-start limit only; the loss of clock coherence by the level-dependent force and by the level-dependent velocity (10.25) is not treated.

For profiles of the field that are not linear the phase of the hopping depends on x; its effect is given only as the change of the start of Step 2(b), and the velocity (10.24), (10.25) is derived for the linear profiles.

Where 2ε_1 + 2ε_2 + ε_3 ≥ 1 (a slow field, or ε_3 not small) only the R0 statements (10.1), (10.2), (10.4) and the first part of (10.7) are derived; whether an effective description exists there is not determined, except for ε = 0, where it is exact.

consistency_checks.check: Dimensions: γ_x is an inverse cost, γ_x·M_k² a cost, ρ·M_k², γ^(3)·M_k², γ_1·M_k and β·M_k² pure numbers like g, accelerations and defects τ² times a number as in (4.16); κ⟨X⟩/M_k and the hopping phase are pure numbers, the velocity τ²·M_k·ρ_Y a cost; μ_{x,k} is a cost, Ξ·d²·λ a pure number; γ_0·Σ, D_0 and λ_0·r̄ are pure numbers and both sides of (10.36) are τ²/λ_0 times a number.

Sharp field ε = 0 and field operators commuting with C_f: all new coefficients vanish, H_eff equals the compression, the excited component is zero and (2.3) is recovered; (10.22) reduces to (4.16) for the variant (a) with the plain gradient −κ⟨X⟩, level-independent iff ⟨X⟩ = 0 as (4.22) states; the velocity (10.25) vanishes; (P) and (10.28) hold, Ξ = 0, D_0 = 1 and (10.34) is the record defect alone.

Exact on-site problems against the expansion: the cell (second-order term, vanishing third-order term, hopping factor); the two-place field of Step 2(b) (negative rest term); the two-level member of (10.36) (mean rate zero at the order kept, exact value within the margin of (10.35)); (10.34) reduces to (10.17), (10.26) for small γ_0·Σ; the three-place control of (10.40) (the eigenvalue that continues e_0 is exactly the sharp-field value, and the overlap of its eigenvectors for the two branch signs is the hopping factor τ_k/τ).
